title: Made in Canada: Personal Brand, Storytelling and Hybrid Style, with Renée Lindo

host.name: Nola Simon
host.title: Futurist & Founder, Everyday Futurism
host.credentials: 17 years in cross-border insurance operations · Creator of the Assumption-Ground Audit

guest.name: Renée Lindo
guest.title: Personal stylist
guest.credentials: Founder of Let's Get Dressed Now · Former national sales leader in corporate pharmaceuticals

abstract: Renée Lindo, personal stylist and founder of Let's Get Dressed Now, makes the case that style is a tool: what you wear tells your story before you speak, changes what you feel capable of, and can set boundaries when work happens at home. Recorded in late 2021, the conversation names hybrid attire, the balance between comfortable and polished, before most people were back in an office, and covers enclothed cognition, building a wardrobe that is 80% classic and 20% trend, shopping your own closet, and building real relationships on LinkedIn.
takeaways: Run clothing as a boundary when you work from home: get dressed for work to get into work mode, then change when the workday ends, as a switch for your brain and a cue for your family.
Name your personal brand whether you are an employee or an entrepreneur. If how you show up does not match your resume or marketing, people notice the disconnect.
Map your wardrobe at roughly 80% classic, timeless pieces that fit your lifestyle and 20% trends, and let accessories carry personality in a conservative workplace.
Audit your closet before you shop: get rid of what no longer fits your body or your life, and dress for the body you have today.
Surface real relationships behind your network: Renée booked short calls with people who engaged with her content, and many still engage today.

keyQA.question: What is hybrid attire?
keyQA.answer: Renée Lindo's name for clothing that balances comfortable and polished, so you can be on video calls, comfortable at home and ready for the office in the same pieces. She looks for stretch, breathable fabrics, looser cuts and a little structure on top, like a sweater jacket or a blazer over a sweater dress.

keyQA.question: What is enclothed cognition?
keyQA.answer: Research showing that what we wear changes our mood, what we feel we can accomplish and what we feel available for. Renée compares it to putting on a power suit that fits well and is in your best colour: there is nothing magical in the suit, but it changes how you show up.

keyQA.question: How do you mix fast fashion with quality pieces?
keyQA.answer: Renée recommends about 80% classic, timeless pieces that fit your lifestyle and personality, and about 20% trends to keep things current. Even pieces from fast-fashion retailers can last if they suit your body and you love them, so look at the fabric and buy what you will wear for a long time.

keyQA.question: How can clothes help set boundaries when you work from home?
keyQA.answer: Put on work clothes when you start work and change into home clothes when you finish. It is a switch that tells your brain you are off, and a visual cue for your family that you are working and need quiet.
